# Your cloud. Your terminal.

Meet Lazy AWS. A keyboard-driven home for your AWS resources.  
 Browse, inspect, and act. Without the console shuffle.

Get started Take a quick tour

lazyaws — demo

Real Lazy AWS EC2 demo. Resource lists appear beside the selected resource’s JSON details.

Real interface. Sample resources.Made for your keyboard.

## Less setup. More getting things done.

We support macOS, Ubuntu, Arch Linux, and Omarchy. Windows is not supported.

Before you startAWS CLI v2 [...] ### Connect your account

   Use an existing AWS CLI profile. Sign in first if your profile uses SSO.

   terminal

   ```
   aws sso login --profile dev lazyaws --profile dev --region eu-west-1
   ```

## A small learning curve. A lot less clicking.

Three stops. Then you know your way around.

1. 1

   ### Find your bearings.

   Switch services, move between panes, and select a resource. Your account and region stay in view.

   Lazy AWS EC2 demo with instance, volume, security group, and subnet panes beside JSON details.View demo capture
2. 2

   ### Go one level deeper.

   Filter a list, then open the selected resource’s JSON details. Related resources are right beside it.

   Lazy AWS demo with the EC2 JSON detail pane focused.View demo capture
3. 3

   ### Know what will run. [...] Before you startAWS CLI v2

Choose curl or Homebrew to install on macOS or Linux. Then run the demo or connect your AWS account. Debian installs are available without a support guarantee. AWS CLI v2 and credentials are needed only for your AWS account.

1. 1

   ### Install with curl

   Install the binary to ~/.local/bin. Add this directory to your PATH if needed.

   terminal

   ```
   curl -fsSL  | sh
   ```
2. 2

   ### Or install with Homebrew

   Install from our tap on macOS or Linux with Homebrew.

   terminal

   ```
   brew install capybara-brain346/tap/lazyaws
   ```
3. 3

   ### Run the installed demo

   Start with local sample data. No AWS account or credentials needed.

   terminal

   ```
   lazyaws --demo
   ```

Hey Everyone 👋 I live in the terminal. I write code in Neovim and use lazygit, lazydocker and other TUIs every day. But each time I had to work with AWS, I had to leave the terminal for the console or type long CLI commands just to answer simple questions. Which instances are running? What is in this bucket? Did that Lambda deploy? I wanted the lazygit feel for AWS too, so I built my own: Lazy AWS. What it does: - Browse EC2, ECS, ECR, S3 and Lambda in one terminal UI - Filter lists, see related resources and read the full JSON details - Run actions such as stopping an instance or uploading a file, always with a confirmation step Try it in 10 seconds: $ brew install capybara-brain346/tap/lazyaws $ lazyaws
